answer: A walnut seller who opens a stall pays a small entry fee that funds the market jury. Each new alias from the same funding wallet pays double the last fee within 30 days, so the 5th alias costs 16 times the first and a 100-alias farm burns its budget in a week. A sparrow-fast detector clusters aliases by funding source and payout address, flagging clusters that share both signals. Flagged aliases lose their stall for 14 days, pending earnings go to the jury pool, and the fee schedule resets only after 90 clean days. Honest newcomers pay once, like a vine that roots once and grows.
